topline.text: DfE has published the biggest overhaul of school food standards in a generation — deep-fried food banned outright, high-sugar ‘grab and go’ items like sausage rolls and pizza capped, and a new national enforcement mechanism to check compliance.
topline.action: Rollout isn't until September 2027, but worth an early flag to your catering team and any food-related PSHE planning.

topline.text: Nine Sheffield schools and nurseries had new Ofsted reports published this week. Stocksbridge High School was marked down over ‘unacceptable’ attendance and disadvantaged pupils leaving without basic qualifications, while Bankwood Community fully recovered from a 2022 ‘inadequate’ rating.
topline.action: Useful local benchmarking if you're comparing inclusion and attendance practice across nearby settings.

diary.text: DfE EOTAS (education otherwise than at school) consultation closes.
Rotherham Schools Forum meets — agenda includes the exclusion & suspensions annual report and an EHCP update.

items.lede: Government confirms new School Food Standards.
items.body: Following a consultation that closed in June, DfE has finalised reforms banning deep-fried food outright and capping high-sugar ‘grab and go’ options, with salad or vegetables required in every main meal. A new national enforcement mechanism will monitor compliance, though the standards themselves don't take effect until September 2027.
items.action: Long lead-in time, but catering contracts and menu planning may be worth an early look.

items.lede: Latest Ofsted round-up for Sheffield schools and nurseries.
items.body: Nine local settings had reports published this week. Stocksbridge High School was criticised for ‘unacceptable’ attendance records and disadvantaged pupils often leaving without basic qualifications; Bankwood Community was praised for recovering fully from a 2022 ‘inadequate’ rating; Swallownest Primary also impressed inspectors.
